summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump's peace envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv over weekend, Not a mistrial, yet. Clancy's lawyer asks for emergency appeal in her murder trial, and Investigation launched into polling firm at centre of Reform UK allegations. Across BBC, NPR, and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are clancy, reform, and lindsay. In the background, Lindsay Clancy murder trial: jury says with ‘heavy heart’ it cannot reach unanimous verdict – live updates and Reform suspends two officials over donations sting as Farage admits their comments ‘don’t look good’ – UK politics live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump's peace envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv over weekend
headlines.description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have led President Donald Trump's efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war - but talks have stalled.

headlines.title: Not a mistrial, yet. Clancy's lawyer asks for emergency appeal in her murder trial
headlines.description: The judge was on the verge of declaring a mistrial in Lindsay Clancy's murder case. Then her defense attorney requested time to seek an emergency stay from the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts.

headlines.title: Investigation launched into polling firm at centre of Reform UK allegations
headlines.description: British Polling Council and Market Research Society announce inquiries into JL Partners, which has been accused of breaking transparency rules What is the latest finance scandal facing Reform UK? A polling firm at the centre of allegations that Reform UK breached electoral law is being investigated by two industry bodies. JL Partners, which is run by former Conservative aides, has been accused of breaking transparency rules by failing to declare that three separate polls had been commissioned by the party.

headlines.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial: jury says with ‘heavy heart’ it cannot reach unanimous verdict – live updates
headlines.description: Jury returns to tell judge for a third time it cannot reach a verdict in case of Massachusetts woman who killed her children Judge set to declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy case after jury deadlocked third time If a mistrial is declared, the prosecution could decide to pursue a retrial and try again with a new jury, or they could offer a plea deal to Lindsay Clancy ’s attorney. They could also decide to drop the case. When asked on Wednesday about the prospect of a retrial, Clancy’s lawyer Kevin Reddington had said he was prepared to “try the case next week”.

headlines.title: Reform suspends two officials over donations sting as Farage admits their comments ‘don’t look good’ – UK politics live
headlines.description: James Orr and Dan Jukes, aides to Nigel Farage, stepped down after an investigation by Channel 4 News British ministers have hit back after the Argentinian president said “winds of change” favourable to his country’s claim to the Falklands were “blowing around the world”, Kiran Stacey reports. The Electoral Commission has issued a statement this morning saying it is in touch with the police about the undercover investigation into Reform UK. In a statement, it said: We are considering all relevant information, in line with our regulatory remit, and we are in touch with the Met police. The Electoral Commission has not approved the donor vetting process for Reform, or any other party. Parties are responsible for ensuring their internal processes and controls are fit for purpose.

headlinePool.title: Trump threatens to halt trade with some countries unless the Federal Reserve lowers interest rates – US politics live
headlinePool.description: Trump appears to be picking up interest rate fight again with new Fed chief after long-running feud with previous incumbent Trump cited August’s strong jobs report as sufficient justification to lower rates, and warned that, if the central bank didn’t go along, he’d halt trade between the US and any nations with which it maintains a trade deficit.

headlinePool.title: Judge set to declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy case after jury deadlocked again
headlinePool.description: Defense lawyer has asked for an hour to request emergency stay after jury deadlocked for third time Lindsay Clancy murder trial: live updates The judge in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three young children, plans to declare a mistrial after the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict and remained deadlocked after a week of deliberations . Jurors in Plymouth state court spent more than 38 hours in deliberations over the charges against the 36-year-old mom, which came on the heels of a weeks-long trial that directed national attention to maternal mental health issues that can occur postpartum.

headlinePool.title: Russia strikes Ukraine intelligence HQ in ‘major escalation’
headlinePool.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he has told SBU to deliver ‘appropriate, tangible response’ to Kyiv strike The head office of Ukraine’s SBU intelligence agency has been hit in a Russian drone attack, sending plumes of black smoke rising into the air in the heart of Kyiv. Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he had instructed the SBU to deliver an “appropriate, tangible response” to the strike, while the foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, described it as a “major escalation”.

headlinePool.title: Canary staff not paid amid fears for news website’s future
headlinePool.description: Outlet faced significant financial challenges after it had funds blocked by bank without explanation Workers at the leftwing news outlet the Canary fear it will not survive beyond this year amid access to funds being blocked and allegations of financial mismanagement and internal turmoil. The site, which was founded in 2015 against a backdrop of the wave of support for the then Labour leader, Jeremy Corbyn, appeared set to expand after a multimillion-pound injection of funds last year.

headlinePool.title: New York City police fatally shoot man who climbed up Brooklyn Bridge cables
headlinePool.description: Officers clipped to bridge had tried to talk man, who was holding a knife, into coming down safely, officials say New York City police shot and killed a man on Friday morning after he climbed on to the cables of the Brooklyn Bridge and approached officers with a knife extended, New York police department officials said. At a news conference on Friday, NYPD officials said that a 911 call came in at around 3.28am on Friday morning, reporting that a man was walking on the beams of the Brooklyn Bridge.

headlinePool.title: Germany urges EU to cut Russians’ holiday visas after sabotage attacks
headlinePool.description: Belarusian said to have had tourist visa issued by Italy is investigated over alleged attempt to attack Leipzig airport Europe live – latest updates Germany is urging its European partners to introduce tighter limitations on Russian citizens entering the EU on tourist visas, after recent sabotage attacks which Berlin has blamed on Moscow . German authorities are investigating a Belarusian national, who also holds a Russian passport, over the alleged attempt to attack Leipzig airport using drones and explosives.

headlinePool.title: Deadlocked jury in Lindsay Clancy trial resumes deliberations after dispute
headlinePool.description: Jury starts seven day of deliberations after foreperson told judge juror won’t follow instruction about reasonable doubt The deadlocked jury in the Lindsay Clancy trial started a seventh day of deliberations on Friday, a day after the jury’s foreperson told the judge a single juror would not follow the court’s instructions about reasonable doubt. The extraordinary disclosure made in the form of a note delivered to the judge offered the clearest glimpse yet of what may be keeping jurors from reaching a verdict on whether the Massachusetts mother is criminally responsible for killing her three children.

headlinePool.title: Israelis shoot dead two Palestinian teenagers after settlers encircle village
headlinePool.description: Troops escort settlers into al-Mughayyir and raze village outside Hebron as ethnic cleansing of West Bank continues Israelis have shot dead two teenagers in a Palestinian village encircled by settlers, and Israeli troops have razed an entire village outside Hebron, in the latest attacks in a surge of Israeli terror and ethnic cleansing across the occupied West Bank. The shootings targeted Khalil Abu Alia, 16, who was about to start 11th grade at the al-Mughayyir boys school, and 19-year-old Omar al-Nassan, who graduated from the same institution with top marks this summer.
